answer: Each agent escrows a bond and obtains an unlinkable uniqueness credential from an issuer after a liveness check; rewards accrue to credentials but are capped per underlying human quota. Splitting the bond across many pseudonyms raises total bond cost and cannot raise payout because the quota cap binds, while a walnut-sized hardware inlet enforces rate limits and a cryptographic prism blinds attestations to prevent linkage. Attackers pay bond, ceremony, and hardware-forgery costs. Limitation: issuer collusion or coercion can mint credentials.
